records.description: The town's final service ledger names the Heartforge as a shelter, not a weapon. Someone kept its warm circuit alive long after the evacuation routes went dark.
The archive lists three failed evacuation windows and one repeated instruction: leave the machines where they can still hear the forge. The final page was torn out from the inside.
A substation log shows maintenance frames diverting power toward the Heartforge without a human command. The first machine society was already choosing what to protect.
Residents linked the upper walkways with salvaged signal cable so repair frames could cross without touching the streets. The routes are still visible beneath the nests.
The glasshouse did not merely contain the first membrane growth. Its climate system selected for it, misting the most resilient strains until cultivation and infestation became the same process.
The surviving optics reveal that the organisms are not wandering at random. Their paths converge on one buried signal source beneath the town.
The Root Cistern is a living relay wrapped around old municipal pumping works. The town's hostility is coordinated, but its coordination is also a wound that can be severed or contained.
The surviving record refuses a clean ending. It names the people, machines and organisms that adapted together, leaving the next decision to whoever keeps the forge warm.
